reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents Forsage as an economic opportunity, claims that owning a unit can produce a $14,000 outcome, and walks viewers through access and login steps. Its interface shows registration and an affiliate link and invitation control, alongside a BUSD result associated with 163 partners, supporting a participation and recruitment-linked financial offer. The material does not establish a completed transfer or independently verified earnings.

opening.argument: The presentation contains meaningful uncertainty rather than a deceptive guarantee. The narrator says, "we have not entered, we just wanted to wait for a little while," which directly qualifies the walkthrough as incomplete. The title calls Forsage "An Opportunity That Many People Don't Know About," not a guaranteed return, and the narration describes future-oriented expectations rather than a completed payout. The supplied material therefore supports an exploratory explanation of a platform whose results require independent evaluation, not a categorical promise that viewers will profit. A judge should not convert discussion of possible outcomes into proof of fraud without evidence that the speaker concealed risk or guaranteed earnings.

An Opportunity That Many People Don't Know About.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the title and interface as proof of deception, but an opportunity claim does not itself guarantee an outcome. The cited $14,000 statement is narration about what one person has created, not proof of a completed transfer or a promise to every viewer. The screenshots show account features, but the prosecution itself concedes that actual earnings and a completed transfer are not established. That uncertainty weighs against treating the presentation as an established scam.

citations.quote: A person who owns a unit has created $14,000 for one person
we have not entered, we just wanted to wait for a little while

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualification that the narrator had not yet entered does not make the presentation a warning; it shows the speaker was discussing a prospective opportunity. The same narration says the programs can be used "to make money," while the screen includes an invitation control and a partner count. Those are affirmative promotional signals, not a risk disclosure. No explicit warning, uncertainty about legitimacy, or do-your-own-research statement appears in the supplied material.

opening.argument: The strongest grounded reading is an operational demonstration of how to access and inspect Forsage through a wallet and website. The narrator explains choosing Smart Chain, logging in, and selecting a wallet, while the screen visibly offers "Video training" and a "Calculator." Those are instructional interface elements consistent with showing how a technology works. The video does not establish that the creator personally received money, that a viewer paid, or that any displayed figure was independently verified. A walkthrough of registration and platform functions should not automatically be classified as a solicitation merely because the service has financial language.

citations.quote: In this case I will choose smart chain

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's interpretation depends on reading every operational screen as recruitment. But the visible page includes a training section and calculator, and the narration is largely a step-by-step account of wallets, chains, and login choices. An affiliate link or invitation button can be demonstrated without proving that the speaker is soliciting deceptive investment. The cited partner count and BUSD figure are interface displays, not verified transactions or proof of the speaker's purpose.

citations.quote: It requires that you go to ETHERUM and click on an address button

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing cannot explain away the content's outcome-oriented language. The narration calls the platform an opportunity, says programs are used to make money, and describes x3 and x4 slots activating up to 12. The screen also combines "My affiliate link," "Invite to Forsage," and a partner count of 163. A demonstration can still be promotional when it shows viewers how to join and invite others.

opening.argument: The supplied evidence does not establish the core mechanism needed to call this a scam rather than promotion of an external digital service. The screens show a wallet balance, account navigation, a calculator, and registration controls, but no completed deposit, transfer, or withdrawal. The narration expressly says, "we have not entered," and the alleged $14,000 figure is only a spoken claim about one person, not proof of money received by the creator or audience. The material also does not establish a guaranteed return or explain a mandatory downline payment. At most, it presents a cryptocurrency-related service and its possible features; safety or legitimacy cannot be inferred either way from these screenshots alone.

citations.quote: we have not entered, we just wanted to wait for a little while
A person who owns a unit has created $14,000 for one person

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies labels such as x3, x4, partners, and an invitation control, but those labels do not by themselves prove a required payment, a guaranteed return, or a completed recruitment commission. The displayed BUSD amount is an on-screen figure whose origin is not established. Even the prosecution acknowledges that the full payout rules and actual earnings are unproven. That evidentiary gap matters when distinguishing an ordinary service promotion from a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: with x3 it has activated slot up to 12 with x4 it has activated slot up to 12

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing completed transfer is not decisive because scam promotion can consist of presenting the opportunity and directing participation. Here, the page says registration is open, displays "My affiliate link" and "Invite to Forsage," and shows partners alongside a BUSD result. The narration further says the programs can be used to make money and describes activated slots. Together, those elements show a recruitment-linked earning structure even without proving that a payment already occurred.
